sections.overview: The Redback is a widow spider common in Australian towns and disturbed places.
sections.identification: Females have a red dorsal stripe; males are smaller and paler.
sections.habitat: It webs in dry shelters such as sheds, shrubs and rock crevices.
sections.behavior: It stays in its web; bites usually follow accidental pressure against skin.
sections.reproduction: Females can store sperm and use it for several egg batches.
sections.ecology: It is closely related to the New Zealand Katipō, Latrodectus katipo; they remain distinct species.
sections.conservation: The sources describe its range and biology, not a global conservation assessment.
